entries.source: Registry note on 0x477010: '死神 status rendered "Doom" per the reconciled system-vocabulary pool (was "the Grim Reaper" in an earlier draft) - "Reaper" reserved for the character-facing sense (e.g. Reaper's Whistle) elsewhere.' Cross-confirmed by the parallel scroll item シニガーミの書 -> 'Scroll of Doom' (0x532f2e), and by 0x4eb650's own note ('...死神->"Doom" were chosen').
entries.usage_note: Term-consistency audit 2026-09-03 (agent1): flagged as a possible inconsistency (Doom at 0x477010/0x477090/0x4770c0/0x4eb650 vs Reaper at 0x4613d0/0x531c1e Reaper's Whistle) but is a DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION per the note above - do not flatten to one word. Use 'Doom' for the status ailment/battle-event sense (someone is possessed by / summons / drives away the death-entity as a game mechanic), 'Reaper' for the character-facing/item-flavor sense (the literal grim-reaper figure and its whistle). Logged, not corrected, in agent1-corrections.csv id 0x477010.

entries.source: Dokapon Kingdom wiki (dokapon.fandom.com/wiki/Job, Category:Jobs); StrategyWiki 'Dokapon Kingdom/Jobs' page - the Dokapon series' official English localization uniformly calls the class/profession system 'Job(s)' (Warrior, Magician, Thief, Cleric, etc.), confirmed via web search 2026-09-03
entries.usage_note: Term-consistency audit 2026-09-03 (agent2): 66 occurrences of 職業 in the registry, 59 already say 'Job'/'Jobs' consistently. 7 outliers in the navi_intro pool's character-creation flow (charcreate-05-class-q, charcreate-09-class-q-alt, and the 5 charcreate-*-class-tooltip-* entries: fighter/mage/tank/speed/freelancer) said 'class' instead - corrected to 'Job'/'job' per the owner's align-to-majority rule; see agent2-corrections.csv ids 0x4efeb0, 0x4effa0, 0x4f0390, 0x4f0400, 0x4f0470, 0x4f04d0, 0x4f0540. No note on any of the 7 documented a deliberate reason to keep 'class', so this is a straightforward majority-alignment fix, not an exception.

entries.source: Term-consistency audit 2026-09-03 (agent2): 28 of 29 occurrences render 犯罪者 as 'criminal'/'criminals' (one is the standalone menu label 'Criminal', 0x538428, title-cased as expected for a label)
entries.usage_note: DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION, not flattened: entry 0x4eb650 (help-manual-page, event help-page-18-field-ailments, a status-ailment list block) deliberately renders 犯罪者 as 'Wanted' instead. Its own `note` field explicitly says: 'See glossary section above for why コロリ->"Plague" and 死神->"Doom" and 犯罪者->"Wanted" were chosen' - a reasoned register choice for that ailment-list context (matches the list's other short status-name style: Poison, Plague, Hobbled, Sealed, Doom, Sleep). Left as-is per the owner's exception rule; do not correct it to 'Criminal'.

entries.source: Term-consistency audit 2026-09-03 (agent2): matches the formal item name 'Suspicious Package' (id 0x531c6e, jp 怪しい荷物) that this word refers to throughout the smuggling/courier quest chain (morude, musashi-courier, inquisitor-sermon, hint-npcs event pools)
entries.usage_note: 5 of 7 occurrences already say 'package' (Morude's delivery-quest dialogue, Musashi the courier's dialogue, and the item label itself). 2 outliers said 'cargo' instead, describing the exact same in-quest item ('suspicious cargo' / 'this cargo') - corrected to 'package' for consistency with the majority and the formal item name. See agent2-corrections.csv ids 0x486af0 (hint-npcs-026) and 0x48ab30 (inquisitor-sermon-012).

entries.source: Term-consistency audit 2026-09-03 (agent3); majority convention across registry/string-registry.json (~95 of 99 マス occurrences already render Panel/panels)
entries.usage_note: The board-game grid square/tile a player lands on. source_pool=pool_b_gameplay used 'Space' in 12 entries (0x4795a0, 0x4795e0, 0x479620, 0x479d40, 0x479d70, 0x479d90, 0x479ee0, 0x479f20, 0x479f60, 0x47d100, 0x47d1c0, 0x486670) - a known structural drift in that pool, not a coincidence. Realigned all 12 to 'Panel' per the owner's majority-wins rule; none carried a note documenting 'Space' as a deliberate choice. Distance-count idioms like 'move 0 to 6 spaces' (0x460c20) are a different construction (counting travel units, not naming the landable square) and were left alone.

entries.source: Term-consistency audit 2026-09-03 (agent3); 5 of 6 occurrences already 'Collection Panel(s)' (0x4e8560, 0x4e8cb0, 0x4ec830, 0x5388e0, 0x5388f0 'All-Village Collection Panel')
entries.usage_note: The panel type where a ruler collects tribute from owned villages/towns/cities (distinct from the 'collect from everywhere at once' panel, which explicitly contrasts itself against 'a Collection Panel' at 0x4e8cb0). 0x479ee0 (pool_b_gameplay) used 'Collect Funds' instead - same structural drift as the マス/Panel case above. Its own note frames 'Collect Funds' only as a fix over an earlier mistranslation ('Toll'), not a reasoned choice to diverge from 'Collection Panel', so realigned to majority.

entries.source: Term-consistency audit 2026-09-03 (agent3); cross-checked against the full 大神殿入口/大神殿内部/大神殿最深部 dungeon-label family (15 entries) and the ムー大神殿 root term
entries.usage_note: Elliptical dungeon-label form (JP omits explicit 'ムー'/Mu). Consistently drops both 'Grand' and 'Mu', rendering just 'the Temple Depths' (mid-sentence) / 'Temple Depths' (standalone label) / 'Temple Depths Panel' (マス-suffixed panel label) - mirrors 大神殿入口 -> 'the Temple Entrance' and 大神殿内部 -> 'the Temple Interior', both of which show the identical explicit-Mu-vs-elliptical split. The full form 'ムー大神殿' (JP explicitly includes Mu) instead renders 'the Grand Temple of Mu' (0x52f670, 0x4e92d0, 0x4e9e70, 0x4ec660, 0x538a60 'Grand Temple of Mu Entrance', 0x538d70 'Grand Temple of Mu Exit'). 0x4ea090 ('大神殿最深部マス', no ムー, was 'Grand Temple Depths Panel') incorrectly applied the full-form naming: its own note claims to 'match the Grand Temple of Mu naming used throughout the dungeon-label entries below', but on verification the actual dungeon-label entries below use the SHORT 'Temple X' form, and the directly parallel sibling 0x538fd0 ('大神殿入口マス' -> 'Temple Entrance Panel', not 'Grand Temple of Mu Entrance Panel') confirms the マス-panel-label form should also drop 'Grand'/'Mu'. The note's stated reasoning does not hold up against the actual pattern, so it is not treated as a valid documented exception; realigned to 'Temple Depths Panel'.

entries.usage_note: 3 of 7 occurrences (0x487dd0 x2 internal uses, 0x489d30, 0x4d1310) used 'devil'/'devils' instead of the majority 'demon' (4 of 7: 0x486e90, 0x4870c0, 0x487760, 0x4d0ce0). No note documents 'devil' as a deliberate register choice - realigned to 'demon' to match both the within-term majority and the pre-existing あくま lock.

entries.source: Term-consistency audit 2026-09-03 (agent3); matches the formal, highlighted stat-definition usage in the help-manual page (0x4eb040, capitalized 5x while formally introducing the mechanic) and the battle-system level-up message (0x457db0)
entries.usage_note: A named job stat (5 ranks; raises salary; persists across job changes). 4 of 6 occurrences, all in casual/dialect NPC advice dialogue (0x4859f0 Osaka dialect, 0x485ef0 アル-dialect, 0x4862f0, 0x487290), paraphrased the same mechanic as 'skill'/'skill level(s)' instead - no note documents this as deliberate (unlike, e.g., the genuinely documented 死神 Doom/Reaper split found elsewhere in this audit). Realigned the 4 casual lines to 'Proficiency' so the same game mechanic reads as the same stat name in dialogue, the help page, and battle messages, while keeping each line's dialect flavor intact.

entries.source: Term-consistency audit 2026-09-03 (agent3); 6 of 7 occurrences already render 金額 as 'amount'
entries.usage_note: General term for a sum of gold (e.g. a target amount, a deposited amount). The settings-screen label 0x4ef210 ('目標金額', was 'Target Money||') is paired with the description text at 0x4ebf60 ('...a target amount of gold to reach') for the same Free Mode win-condition setting - the label used 'Money' while its own description used 'amount', an internal label/description mismatch. No note documents 'Money' as deliberate (it only explains the string's byte-shape, mirroring sibling 0x4ef1f0 '目標期間' -> 'Target Period'). Realigned the label to 'Target Amount'.

entries.source: Term-consistency audit 2026-09-03 (agent4, docs/audits/2026-09/term-consistency-audit.json); resolves a standalone-label vs. narration split across battle-status-messages-1/2, vocab-status-effects, battle-status-labels, and help-manual-page
entries.usage_note: As a standalone status-ailment/UI label, render 封印 as 'Seal' (noun) - matches 0x534796 'Seal', 0x538408 'Seal', 0x53498e 'Attack Magic Seal', 0x53499e 'Defense Magic Seal', and the combo label 0x4d9dd0 'Cowardice & Seal'. The help-manual field-ailments list entry (0x4eb650) previously used 'Sealed' for this same label slot; corrected to 'Seal' to match. This label convention is separate from 封印's narration/verb-or-adjective uses (e.g. 'had their magic sealed!', "'s magic is sealed...", "'s seal was broken!", 'the roads...are sealed'), which correctly vary in grammatical form by sentence role and are NOT an inconsistency - do not flatten those to match the label.

entries.source: Term-consistency audit 2026-09-03 (agent4, docs/audits/2026-09/term-consistency-audit.json); resolves a 3-way standalone-label split (Money / Gold Held / Gold on Hand) across the battle_system, pool_b_gameplay, misc_labels, and help_and_events source pools
entries.usage_note: As a standalone UI stat label for 'the gold you're carrying', use 'Gold' as the head noun. Surrounding scaffolding may still vary naturally by widget - 'Gold Held' for a comparison-table column header (0x47a550, 0x487f40), 'Gold on Hand' to parallel 'Vault'/'Specialty Goods'/'Village Value' in the Total Assets help-manual breakdown (0x4eb290), bare 'Gold:' in the end-of-turn stat summary (0x4eeb00) - but the head word must be 'Gold', matching the game's established currency term (see glossary entry ゴールド -> Gold, official/locked) and the 13+ narrative 'Current gold:' instances that were already consistent. The battle Steal/Discard-command category labels (0x4592e0, 0x459300, 0x459b60) and their matching skill descriptions (0x459660, 0x459d40) previously rendered this 'Money' instead; corrected to 'Gold' for consistency. 0x538450 ('Money: 0') had also deliberately matched that now-corrected 'Money' precedent per its own note - carried forward to 'Gold: 0' to stay consistent with the corrected precedent, since the note's own stated rationale was alignment, not an independent defense of 'Money'.
